title: search's prose form prints a hit's section label, not the line that matched
body:
`intent search "expired snapshot" --limit 3` prints, for the hit at `docs/reference/commands.md:62`, the row's name (`` `intent backup` ``, the section label) and not the line that matched. The JSON for the same query carries `"snippet": "Snapshot this machine's store -- prunes expired snapshots; one-way, no restore verb ships"`, which is the match. So the prose form shows a reader where a hit is and hides what matched, and for a whiteboard hit the name printed is the whole entry heading. Print the snippet (or both, name then snippet), so a text search's answer can be read without `--json`.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): the prose form prints the snippet after the name when they differ. After: `docs/reference/commands.md:63  file  docs/reference/commands.md  \`intent backup\`  Snapshot this machine's store -- prunes expired snapshots; ...`.
